headline: Quantum Bounds, Anyons, and Algorithmic Warm-Starts
summary: Today's papers explore the boundaries and applications of quantum systems across measurement theory, condensed matter, and optimization. Researchers establish exact mathematical bounds for global versus local quantum observables, demonstrate anyon-impurity bound states for controlled braiding, and leverage low-depth quantum algorithms to accelerate classical optimization solvers.

themes.title: Quantum Measurement & Information Bounds
themes.body: A Lean-verified proof establishes a sharp constant bound of √2 min(n,m) comparing global and local product measurement norms in bipartite quantum systems, tightening quantum data hiding limits.

themes.title: Topological Anyon Engineering
themes.body: Combining analytical models and Harper-Hofstadter simulations shows that binding a mobile impurity to a quasihole in fractional Chern insulators enables direct measurement of fractional charge and controlled anyon braiding.

themes.title: Quantum-Classical Hybrid Optimization
themes.body: Low-depth QAOA circuits generate local correlators to warm-start classical rank-two MaxCut relaxations, accelerating convergence to high-quality solutions on graphs up to 1000 qubits.

connections.body: While 2608.06235 mathematically bounds the fundamental norm gap between global and local product observables, 2608.06212 practically exploits local quantum correlators to guide classical optimization solvers.
